title: Why AI bubble fears aren't keeping this Amazon boss up at night
source_used: Yahoo Finance (original URL, read in full)
key_facts: Amazon Web Services chief executive Matt Garman said on an Andreessen Horowitz podcast that AI bubble fears are not keeping him up at night.
He said AWS takes a diversified approach so not all capacity is tied to one customer, and that most usage is core compute, storage and inference that 'just aren't gonna go away'.
He compared AI to the venture-capital model, where not every billion-dollar start-up makes it, and to the internet bubble, after which the internet remained.
AWS exited the second quarter with a backlog of nearly $500 billion.
AI bubble talk is returning as Nvidia, AMD, Marvell and Micron shares hit record highs.
Nvidia, Apple and Microsoft now make up over 21% of the S&P 500, per Creative Planning, the most concentrated in three stocks on record.
Ray Dalio warned this week that AI speculation may be nearing its peak.
quote_evidence: "We feel really good about the spend we're making now," Garman said in a new podcast posted on the YouTube page of venture capital outfit Andreessen Horowitz.
Billionaire Bridgewater Associates founder Ray Dalio warned this week that AI speculation may be nearing its peak.

The S&P 500 (^GSPC) has never been more concentrated in just three stocks than it is today, with Nvidia, Apple (AAPL), and Microsoft (MSFT) representing over 21% of the index, per data from Creative Planning.
why_it_matters_hint: The head of the biggest cloud provider says demand for AI computing is durable, while others warn of a peak.
event_date: podcast date not stated; reported 9 Oct 2026
notes: A company executive's own view; the podcast was not opened. The article misspells his name once as 'Garmin'.
